title: The Fond look from the door
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：fond　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fond 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the baker wrote of ① a fond look from the door in the bill, and everybody in the bakery said at once that it was ② fonder than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the baker, who never explained anything, had done it on the same day and gone home; it was the fond ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the fondest look from the door anybody in the bakery had ever seen, or so the bill for December 1967 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too fond to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the customer who had come to help; the fond ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the tray at the far oven, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a fond memory of the place, and said that no customer in his right mind would call it ⑥ as fond as the memory of the place they had once had in the old bakery. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was fond or not, and he said so.

By 1980 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the bill. What the line asked for was ⑦ something fond, and nothing besides. The customer from the next bakery called the whole plan ⑧ quite fond; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the bill kept the names of the fond ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1983, before dawn, she wrote of another fond look from the door in the same bill, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ fonder than anybody had expected. ⑩ The fondest memory of the place in the whole bakery, she said in 1985, was the one she could never quite name; the fond ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 喜爱（前置定语 a fond look from the door：1973 年面点师在账单里记下的那件喜爱的目光）
B. adj. 喜爱／慈爱（比较级 fonder than：文中两处，一处比门口慈爱的目光，一处比预想）
C. adj. 喜爱／慈爱（最高级 the fondest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 喜爱（表语 too fond to do：母亲觉得它太喜爱，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 慈爱（前置定语 a fond memory of the place：叔叔把整件事称作一桩慈爱的美好回忆）
F. adj. 慈爱（同级比较 as fond as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩对那地方的美好回忆相比）
G. adj. 慈爱（后置定语 something fond：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 慈爱（受程度副词修饰 quite fond：那位顾客的评价）

items.q: a fond look from the door
the fondest look from the door anybody
a fond memory of the place
The fondest memory of the place in

answers.why: fond 意为“喜爱”，1973 年面点师在账单里记下的是“一件喜爱的目光”，此处作前置定语 a fond look from the door。
fond 意为“喜爱”，此处用比较级 fonder than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
fond 意为“喜爱”，账单上 十二月 那行字说它是糕饼铺里最喜爱的一件，故用最高级 the fondest look from the door。
fond 意为“喜爱”，母亲认为这件东西“太喜爱了，谁也用不上”，too fond to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
fond 意为“慈爱”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩慈爱的美好回忆”，此处作前置定语 a fond memory of the place。
fond 意为“慈爱”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩对那地方的美好回忆一样慈爱”，同级比较用 as fond as。
fond 意为“慈爱”，账单上那半行字要的是“慈爱的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something fond。
fond 意为“慈爱”，邻糕饼铺来的那位顾客认为这套计划“相当慈爱”，quite 修饰原级 fond。
fond 意为“慈爱”，1983 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要慈爱”，故用比较级 fonder than。
fond 意为“慈爱”，母亲 1985 年说的是“整个糕饼铺里最慈爱的那一桩”，故用最高级 the fondest memory of the place。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1973 年，面点师在账单里记下了一件喜爱的目光。（a fond look from the door）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更喜爱。（fonder than …）
母亲觉得它太喜爱，谁也用不上。（too fond to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩慈爱的美好回忆。（a fond memory of the place）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩对那地方的美好回忆一样慈爱。（as fond as …）
到了 1980 年，账单上只剩半行字：要的是一件慈爱的东西。（something fond）
answers: In 1973 the baker wrote of a fond look from the door in the bill.
Everybody said it was fonder than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too fond to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a fond memory of the place.
He said nobody would call it as fond as the memory of the place they had once had.
By 1980 the bill asked for nothing but something fond.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 fond 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the baker wrote of a fond look from the door in the bill, and nobody forgot it.
It was the fondest look from the door in the bakery, or so the bill says.
My mother thought it too fond to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a fond memory of the place, and nobody argued with him.
The customer from the next bakery called the plan quite fond, and everybody laughed.
The fond ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
